sent_messages:
Funnel drop diagnosis (demo_funnel.csv, Sep vs Oct 2026):

WHERE it dropped: the drop is at the checkout→payment stage, NOT cart→checkout. cart→checkout is flat (39.94% → 39.91%, −0.03pp). Overall payment CVR fell 52.63% → 51.36% (−1.27pp); purchase conversion rose slightly (+0.24pp).

Root cause: the drop is concentrated in segment A_ios. Its payment-stage conversion fell 60.15% → 55.09% (−5.06pp). B_android is essentially stable (45.11% → 44.44%, −0.67pp). Decomposing the −1.27pp overall payment drop: within-segment effect −2.86pp (driven almost entirely by A_ios), mix effect +2.25pp (traffic shifted toward A_ios, which converts higher at payment), interaction −0.66pp. So the mix shift MASKED ~2.2pp of the real deterioration — the underlying A_ios payment regression is larger than the headline drop.

Recommended next step: drill into A_ios payment failures — break down by device/OS version, payment method, and payment error/failure codes; check whether an iOS app build, payment SDK, or payment provider changed around early Oct; and verify A_ios payment event tracking/logging didn't change (a tracking/attribution artifact is a real candidate).

Data caveats: (1) the CSV contains duplicated date rows — Sep 1st/2nd appear twice, Oct 1st/2nd/3rd appear twice — which inflate absolute user totals but not conversion rates (identical per-segment ratios), so rates and the mix/within decomposition remain valid; (2) October data ends at 10-28; confirm the window is directly comparable before committing to the −1.27pp headline.
